results.content:
## Why Provision for your AI email agent

 Real inbox per agent at @provisionagents.com (or your domain on enterprise).
 Deliverability handled — SPF, DKIM, DMARC, IP warmup, monitoring.
 Inbound parsing and reply routing built in.
 Same agent across email, Slack, Telegram, Discord, and Web Chat — one identity, one memory.
 Daily digest in Slack so you see results without seeing the work.
 Escalation to humans on judgment calls, with full context.
 Open source core — audit or self-host.
 $299/agent. 48-hour free trial.

## FAQ

What is an AI email agent? [...] ## How a Provision AI email agent works

Setup is one click. Operationally, here's what happens day to day with an agent like Echo (Inbox & Outreach) running on Provision.

1. ### 1. Provision creates the inbox

   When you onboard the agent, Provision allocates an address (e.g., echo@provisionagents.com), configures SPF/DKIM/DMARC, and warms the IP reputation. You don't touch DNS or SMTP.
2. ### 2. The agent sends from their address

   When you ask the agent to follow up on yesterday's signups in Slack, they draft and send the emails from their address. Recipients see "From: Echo " — not your name.
3. ### 3. Replies come back to the agent [...] How does the AI email agent decide who to reply to?

It reads incoming mail, classifies by topic and urgency using your team's training (which it learns from a few weeks of work), drafts replies for routine cases, and escalates anything ambiguous to you in Slack with full context. You stay in the loop on judgment calls; the agent handles the rest.

Is the email agent a separate tool from the Slack agent?

No — same agent, multiple surfaces. The marketing agent ("Buzz") that lives in your Slack also has buzz@provisionagents.com. They're one identity with one memory across both channels. A reply that comes in via email becomes context the agent uses next time you @-mention them in Slack.

results.title: 5 Best AgentMail Alternatives I’ve Tested in 2026
results.content:
Extra emails start at $1.80 per 1,000 on Basic, $1.30 per 1,000 on Foundation, and $1.10 per 1,000 on Scale. The trade-off is that Mailgun gives you more control over how application email is handled, but you have to build the agent inbox experience yourself.

## 5. Mailtrap – Best AgentMail Alternative for Testing Agent Emails

Mailtrap homepage

This image shows the Mailtrap homepage

Mailtrap is a direct AgentMail alternative if your AI agents need their own inboxes, but you also want to test their emails before they reach real recipients. Like AgentMail, you can create inboxes for individual agents, receive incoming emails, keep replies in threads, process attachments, and respond through an API. [...] Pro also includes spending controls to manage additional charges. OpenMail is a better fit if you want to add AI agent inboxes one at a time and pay for the extra usage. However, if you need dedicated IPs, you'll still need a custom Enterprise plan, just like with AgentMail.

## 3. Resend – Best AgentMail Alternative for Email APIs and Automations

Resend homepage

This image shows the Resend homepage

Resend is a good AgentMail alternative if you want AI agents to handle emails alongside your application's regular email needs. Like AgentMail, Resend lets you create inboxes, receive messages, manage threads, and send replies through an API. But Resend goes further with features that AgentMail doesn't focus on. [...] ### It's being carefully crafted by AI

Please check your mailbox in 5 minutes

## 2. OpenMail – Best AgentMail Alternative for Affordable AI Agent Inboxes

AgentMail's $20/month Developer plan includes 10 inboxes. To get more, its next plan costs $200/month. OpenMail offers more flexible pricing, starting at €9/month for 10 inboxes, with additional inboxes costing €1 each per month.

OpenMail homepage

This image shows the OpenMail homepage

Like AgentMail, OpenMail lets AI agents send emails, receive replies, manage threads, and process attachments through an API. It also supports webhooks and WebSockets for incoming messages, sender allow/block rules, and direct integrations with OpenClaw, Hermes, and Claude Code.

results.content:
Meets you where you prefer to work: To use Town, you don’t need to learn a new client (like with Shortwave or Superhuman) or install an extension to an existing inbox (like SaneBox or MailMaestro). You can just chat with your Townie through any of your preferred channels between email, Slack, WhatsApp, Telegram, and SMS.
 Routines bring Town beyond just inbox management: The library of prebuilt Routines makes Townies useful out of the box, and creating a new Routine is as simple as describing what you want to do. Routines allow you to do a wider array of possible tasks across different tools in your stack. [...] Town is the newest tool on this list, having launched in June 2026. The idea is that you get your personalized and named AI assistant (called a “Townie”). To extend the assistant metaphor even further, Town assumes that you’ll message your Townie the way you would a coworker. You can reach your Townie in the Town Desktop or iOS app, but you can also send it an email (at its own dedicated @town.com email address), message it on Slack, WhatsApp, or Telegram, or even send it a text message. This is pretty different from most of the other tools on this list, which assume you’re working inside an inbox. [...] If you want a friendly, proactive AI assistant that can manage your inbox, and that you can message with Telegram, SMS, or WhatsApp, look into Town. Just note that more extensive AI features are gated behind the $59/month Pro tier.

If you want one agent that triages your email, briefs you before your meetings, and then goes and does the actual work across the other 250+ apps your job lives in, look into Gumloop. In addition, if you’re a price-conscious open-weight model connoisseur, want to spin the block on the latest frontier model as soon as it’s out, or are just worried about a particular provider reading your emails, Gumloop is the only tool on this list that gives you the full freedom to choose your own models, whenever you want.
